textData.text: No. 4 Ole Miss is expected to be without its most dangerous runner in The Swamp. Star running back Kewan Lacy is not expected to play against No. 21 Florida on Saturday because of a left shoulder injury, Rebels coach Pete Golding
“We still have another chapel session, so I’m not giving up yet,” Golding told ESPN.

Lacy was hurt in last week’s 32-24 win over then-No. 7 LSU. He ran for 43 yards and a touchdown on nine carries before leaving in the third quarter, then had X-rays after the game and an MRI on Sunday, according to ESPN. He was downgraded to doubtful on Friday’s SEC injury report.

Lacy is the engine of the Rebels’ ground game. The junior was an All-American and a Doak Walker Award finalist in 2025, when he set Ole Miss single-season records for carries (306), rushing yards (1,567) and rushing touchdowns (24) in 15 games.

His 2026 season has already been interrupted once. A thigh bruise knocked him out of the opener against Louisville before he returned the next week to score twice against Charlotte. He has 191 yards and four touchdowns on 39 carries this season.

ESPN reported that JT Lindsey and Makhi Frazier will split the carries. Lindsey (No. 26), a sophomore who transferred from LSU, has 48 yards on 12 attempts this season. Frazier (No. 25), a junior transfer from Michigan State, has 38 yards on nine carries.
Together they have 86 yards on 21 carries, about 4.1 yards per attempt. Lacy is averaging 4.9.

Without Lacy, Ole Miss loses the back who averaged just over 20 carries a game a year ago, and more of the load figures to shift to quarterback Trinidad Chambliss. Franz Beard has argued that Florida’s best way to win is to
keep the ball away from Chambliss

Florida has an availability question of its own. Wide receiver Eric Singleton Jr., who has not played this season because of a sprained left ankle, is a game-time decision, though coach Jon Sumrall told ESPN he feels decent about Singleton’s chances. Singleton caught 58 passes for 534 yards and three touchdowns at Auburn in 2025.
Both teams are 3-0 and 1-0 in SEC play. Kickoff is at 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium.
